disclaimer.hi: For educational and informational purposes only. This is not financial or legal advice. Facts are based on public sources as of 23 October 2026; rules may change. Some visuals are illustrative.

title_hi: FREE UPI का बिल कौन भरता है?
title_en: WHO REALLY PAYS FOR YOUR 'FREE' UPI?

lines.display: Every day... 800 million times.
lines.en: Every day... 800 million times.

lines.display: Someone buys a cup of tea. Someone fills up on petrol. Someone sends the rent.
lines.en: Someone buys a cup of tea. Someone fills up on petrol. Someone sends the rent.

lines.display: One QR code. One scan. And in 2 seconds, the money is there.
lines.en: One QR code. One scan. And in 2 seconds, the money is there.

lines.display: No fee. No charge. Completely free.
lines.en: No fee. No charge. Completely free.

lines.display: But the world's largest real-time payment system... does not run for free.
lines.en: But the world's largest real-time payment system... does not run for free.

lines.display: Someone is paying its bill. Every single day.
lines.en: Someone is paying its bill. Every single day.

lines.display: The question is... who?
lines.en: The question is... who?

lines.display: Every magic trick has three parts.
lines.en: Every magic trick has three parts.

lines.display: Part one: the Pledge. The magician shows you something ordinary.
lines.en: Part one: the Pledge. The magician shows you something ordinary.

lines.display: In our story, that ordinary thing is... this.
lines.en: In our story, that ordinary thing is... this.

lines.display: August 2016. NPCI's new system, UPI, goes live for the public with 21 banks.
lines.en: August 2016. NPCI's new system, UPI, goes live for the public with 21 banks.

lines.display: In its first full month, it doesn't even reach 1 million transactions.
lines.en: In its first full month, it doesn't even reach 1 million transactions.

lines.display: Then comes 1 January 2020. The government sets the MDR on UPI and RuPay debit cards to zero.
lines.en: Then comes 1 January 2020. The government sets the MDR on UPI and RuPay debit cards to zero.

lines.display: MDR, the merchant discount rate, is the small fee a shop pays to accept a digital payment. On UPI, it used to be up to 0.30%.
lines.en: MDR, the merchant discount rate, is the small fee a shop pays to accept a digital payment. On UPI, it used to be up to 0.30%.

lines.display: And then... UPI explodes.
lines.en: And then... UPI explodes.

lines.display: September 2026: 24 billion transactions in a single month. More than 800 million, every day.
lines.en: September 2026: 24 billion transactions in a single month. More than 800 million, every day.

lines.display: According to ACI Worldwide, almost half of the world's real-time payments happen in India.
lines.en: According to ACI Worldwide, almost half of the world's real-time payments happen in India.

lines.display: The pledge was kept. UPI was free. Fast. Everywhere.
lines.en: The pledge was kept. UPI was free. Fast. Everywhere.

lines.display: But in magic, what you see... is never the whole truth.
lines.en: But in magic, what you see... is never the whole truth.

lines.display: Part two: the Turn. The magician makes the ordinary thing... disappear.
lines.en: Part two: the Turn. The magician makes the ordinary thing... disappear.

lines.display: In UPI, what disappeared... was the bill.
lines.en: In UPI, what disappeared... was the bill.

lines.display: Behind every scan runs an entire machine: your app, your bank, NPCI, and the shop's bank.
lines.en: Behind every scan runs an entire machine: your app, your bank, NPCI, and the shop's bank.

lines.display: Servers. Security. Fraud checks. Around the clock.
lines.en: Servers. Security. Fraud checks. Around the clock.

lines.display: None of it is free. So when the fee went to zero... where did the cost go?
lines.en: None of it is free. So when the fee went to zero... where did the cost go?

lines.display: Answer number one: the government. In other words, taxpayers.
lines.en: Answer number one: the government. In other words, taxpayers.

lines.display: According to PIB, the government paid banks incentives of ₹1,389 crore in FY22, rising to ₹3,631 crore by FY24.
lines.en: According to PIB, the government paid banks incentives of ₹1,389 crore in FY22, rising to ₹3,631 crore by FY24.

lines.display: But the industry kept saying it wasn't enough. The Payments Council of India said running UPI costs about ₹10,000 crore a year, against government support of just ₹1,500 crore.
lines.en: But the industry kept saying it wasn't enough. The Payments Council of India said running UPI costs about ₹10,000 crore a year, against government support of just ₹1,500 crore.

lines.display: And all this time, the government's answer was the same.
lines.en: And all this time, the government's answer was the same.

lines.display: August 2022. The Finance Ministry: “UPI is a digital public good… There is no consideration in Government to levy any charges.”
lines.en: August 2022. The Finance Ministry: “UPI is a digital public good… There is no consideration in Government to levy any charges.”

lines.display: June 2025. Reports of MDR on UPI? “Completely false, baseless and misleading.”
lines.en: June 2025. Reports of MDR on UPI? “Completely false, baseless and misleading.”

lines.display: Then, just six weeks later, the RBI Governor said: “Costs will have to be paid. Someone will have to bear the cost.”
lines.en: Then, just six weeks later, the RBI Governor said: “Costs will have to be paid. Someone will have to bear the cost.”

lines.display: And in the latest Union Budget, that support was cut by about 10%.
lines.en: And in the latest Union Budget, that support was cut by about 10%.

lines.display: The bill hadn't vanished. It just wasn't visible.
lines.en: The bill hadn't vanished. It just wasn't visible.

lines.display: August 2026. Parliament amends India's payments law.
lines.en: August 2026. Parliament amends India's payments law.

lines.display: 14 September: the Finance Ministry's notification. The next day, the full rulebook.
lines.en: 14 September: the Finance Ministry's notification. The next day, the full rulebook.

lines.display: The rule is simple.
lines.en: The rule is simple.

lines.display: Merchant payments above ₹2,000 carry a 0.4% MDR.
lines.en: Merchant payments above ₹2,000 carry a 0.4% MDR.

lines.display: Even the biggest payment pays no more than ₹300.
lines.en: Even the biggest payment pays no more than ₹300.

lines.display: Railways, telecom, insurance and fuel: a flat ₹5.
lines.en: Railways, telecom, insurance and fuel: a flat ₹5.

lines.display: Person-to-person transfers stay free. And small shops receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month through UPI pay nothing.
lines.en: Person-to-person transfers stay free. And small shops receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month through UPI pay nothing.

lines.display: And the key point: the fee cannot be charged to the customer. The shop pays it.
lines.en: And the key point: the fee cannot be charged to the customer. The shop pays it.

lines.display: NPCI estimates it could raise up to ₹20,600 crore a year.
lines.en: NPCI estimates it could raise up to ₹20,600 crore a year.

lines.display: And then... the countdown began.
lines.en: And then... the countdown began.

lines.display: In a LocalCircles survey of 32,000+ merchants, only 17% said they would absorb the fee themselves.
lines.en: In a LocalCircles survey of 32,000+ merchants, only 17% said they would absorb the fee themselves.

lines.display: And of 67,000+ users, only 14% said they would stick with UPI if the fee were passed on to them.
lines.en: And of 67,000+ users, only 14% said they would stick with UPI if the fee were passed on to them.

lines.display: Petrol pump dealers in Madhya Pradesh announced that from 16 October, they would stop taking UPI above ₹2,000. Dealers in Punjab and Haryana said the same.
lines.en: Petrol pump dealers in Madhya Pradesh announced that from 16 October, they would stop taking UPI above ₹2,000. Dealers in Punjab and Haryana said the same.

lines.display: The case reached the Supreme Court. It refused to pause the fee, and asked the government, the RBI and NPCI to respond.
lines.en: The case reached the Supreme Court. It refused to pause the fee, and asked the government, the RBI and NPCI to respond.

lines.display: And the government's counsel told the court: “It is neither a tax nor a fee.”
lines.en: And the government's counsel told the court: “It is neither a tax nor a fee.”

lines.display: Then, just two days before the deadline, NPCI announced:
lines.en: Then, just two days before the deadline, NPCI announced:

lines.display: The MDR would wait until after Diwali. The new date? Not yet decided.
lines.en: The MDR would wait until after Diwali. The new date? Not yet decided.

lines.display: Part three: the Prestige. The moment the vanished thing comes back.
lines.en: Part three: the Prestige. The moment the vanished thing comes back.

lines.display: The bill that disappeared in 2020... never really disappeared.
lines.en: The bill that disappeared in 2020... never really disappeared.

lines.display: Part of it was paid with taxpayers' money — in other words, your money. The rest was carried by banks and payment companies.
lines.en: Part of it was paid with taxpayers' money — in other words, your money. The rest was carried by banks and payment companies.

lines.display: And now, the bill has come back — to the shopkeeper's counter.
lines.en: And now, the bill has come back — to the shopkeeper's counter.

lines.display: The law says the charge cannot be passed on to you. But every cost a business carries shows up somewhere, eventually, in prices.
lines.en: The law says the charge cannot be passed on to you. But every cost a business carries shows up somewhere, eventually, in prices.

lines.display: So, who pays for free UPI? As a taxpayer: you. As a customer: maybe you. And if the system weakens, the loss is yours too.
lines.en: So, who pays for free UPI? As a taxpayer: you. As a customer: maybe you. And if the system weakens, the loss is yours too.

lines.display: The real question isn't whether UPI should stay free. It's who should pay for this system, and how.
lines.en: The real question isn't whether UPI should stay free. It's who should pay for this system, and how.

lines.display: On one side, a system that needs money to run. On the other, millions of small shopkeepers, and the risk of a return to cash.
lines.en: On one side, a system that needs money to run. On the other, millions of small shopkeepers, and the risk of a return to cash.

lines.display: For now, we wait for the new date. And the case is still pending in the Supreme Court.
lines.en: For now, we wait for the new date. And the case is still pending in the Supreme Court.

lines.display: The coin... is still spinning.
lines.en: The coin... is still spinning.

lines.display: What do you think? Is this fee on payments above ₹2,000 fair, or not? Tell us in the comments. All the sources are in the description.
lines.en: What do you think? Is this fee on payments above ₹2,000 fair, or not? Tell us in the comments. All the sources are in the description.
